title: Facial vein injection of human cells in severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) neonatal mice
author: Pavathuparambil Abdul Manaph, Al-Hawwas, et al.
materials: We used human skin fibroblasts for the injections. The cells were firstly cultured in DMEM with 10% FBS and passaged for 5–6 times, then transfected with a Lentivirus harbouring a red fluorescent protein gene (RFP) at a concentration of 2.5 × 107 particles at 10 mg/ml in 1 ml of culture media. Fresh media was added 24 h post transfection and the cells were visualised for RFP expression by live cell imager (ZOE Fluorescent Cell Imager, Biorad). Cells expressing RFP were sorted and harvested with a cell sorter (FACSAria II Cell Sorter, BD). The human skin fibroblast cell line expressing red fluorescent protein were allowed to expand until the procedure day. The cells were detached from the culture plates using the digestive reagent TrypLE (Thermofisher Scientific, VIC, Australia) and were resuspended in PBS. For each pup, 0.5–1 million cells in 50–100 μl volume were prepared.

steps.title: Prepare fibroblast cell stock
steps.instruction: Culture human skin fibroblasts in DMEM + 10 % FBS, passage 5–6 times, then transfect with lentivirus (2.5 × 10⁷ particles at 10 mg ml⁻¹ in 1 ml media). Add fresh media 24 h post‑transfection, image for RFP expression, sort RFP‑positive cells, expand the sorted line until the day of injection.

steps.title: Create injection cell suspension
steps.instruction: Detach expanded fibroblasts with TrypLE (ThermoFisher), resuspend in PBS, and prepare 0.5–1 × 10⁶ cells in 50–100 µl PBS for each pup.

steps.title: Set up anesthesia chamber
steps.instruction: Place each pup individually in a modified 50 ml tube that has holes on both sides for gas flow; close the tube, connect an isoflurane delivery line (1.5–2.5 % isoflurane in oxygen) through the lid hole, and allow the pup to anesthetize for 5–10 min until immobilised.

steps.title: Load and mark injection needle
steps.instruction: Pre‑load a 29 G insulin needle with the prepared cell suspension and mark the needle tip to prevent excessive depth of insertion.

steps.title: Place pup on warming pad
steps.instruction: After confirming anesthesia, transfer the pup onto a heat pad to maintain body temperature during the injection.

steps.title: Locate and sterilize facial vein
steps.instruction: Under a light source (and a magnifier or microscope if needed) view the partial facial vein near the ear bud; hold the pup so the vein is visible between the index and middle fingers, then wipe the injection site with ethanol while confirming the vein remains visible.

steps.title: Inject cells into vein
steps.instruction: Hold the syringe at a 45° angle, slowly insert the needle tip into the visible vein (blood should be seen through the skin), inject for 5–10 s, then withdraw the needle slowly to prevent back‑flow of the injectate.

steps.title: Confirm injection success
steps.instruction: Observe the injection site: a non‑bolus appearance indicates successful intravascular delivery, whereas a bolus suggests the injection missed the vein.

steps.title: Euthanize and perfuse tissues
steps.instruction: Humanely kill the animal with a pentobarbitone overdose, then perfuse and fix tissues using paraformaldehyde.

steps.title: Fix, cryoprotect, and section organs
steps.instruction: Harvest brain, heart, and liver; fix each organ in 4 % paraformaldehyde for 18–21 h, immerse in 30 % sucrose until the tissue sinks, embed in OCT on a cryomold, freeze, and cut sections of 15–30 µm thickness with a Leica CM3050 S cryostat.

steps.title: Mount sections for fluorescence imaging
steps.instruction: Transfer free‑floating sections to antifreeze solution, wash twice with 1× PBS, mount onto slides with coverslips, and analyse by fluorescent microscopy.
